title: Computer vision
seoTitle: Computer Vision Prototypes & Edge AI | EFIops
metaDescription: Explore camera-based measurement and inspection with a focused computer vision prototype. Python, image processing and edge-device integration around a defined use case.
h1: Turn a visual check into a useful signal.
eyebrow: Computer vision · Test the practical fit
lead: Can a camera help measure an object, spot a condition or create a record for review? Start with a defined task, representative images and a prototype that shows where the approach works—and where it needs help.

sections.heading: Start with the observation you need to make.
paragraphs: A visual task might involve measuring an object, identifying a defect or turning images into records that can be reviewed. The right approach depends on the material, lighting, camera position and the consequences of a wrong result.
A prototype establishes what is practical before a larger deployment is considered.

sections.heading: From sample images to a useful feasibility test.
items: Visual measurement. Explore repeatable measurements under defined conditions.
Defect identification. Test image processing or a suitable model against labelled examples.
Edge processing. Evaluate local analysis on an appropriate device, including Raspberry Pi where it fits.
Workflow output. Connect the result to a review screen, record or reporting process.
Evaluation. Record successful cases, difficult conditions and the limitations of the prototype.

sections.heading: Test the conditions, not only the demonstration.
paragraphs: We define the task, gather representative images and establish a reference for checking results. The prototype is evaluated against variation in the conditions that matter to the use case.
The next step depends on that evidence. Production reliability, maintenance and any sector-specific validation need their own scope.

faqs.question: Have you worked on a real production-related vision project?
faqs.answer: Karol's experience includes a Python and Raspberry Pi application for blueberry size analysis and defect identification. Publication of project materials depends on permission and a clear description of its scope.

faqs.question: Can a prototype be deployed straight into production?
faqs.answer: A prototype establishes feasibility. A live deployment may need additional engineering, evaluation and operational checks.

faqs.question: Will it replace a quality inspector?
faqs.answer: That is not a default assumption. A scoped system may support measurement or review; its appropriate role follows from evaluation and the process requirements.

faqs.question: Can it connect to reporting or another application?
faqs.answer: A suitable output can be designed as part of the prototype so the result is useful beyond the camera view.

cta.label: Discuss a vision prototype
cta.heading: What do you need the camera to recognise or measure?
cta.text: Describe the material, the environment and what the result would be used for.

primaryIntent: computer vision prototype developer; edge AI proof of concept.
summary: Explore camera-based measurement and inspection through a focused, evaluated prototype.

useCases.title: Can we make this check more repeatable?
useCases.body: Set the camera, lighting and reference measurement, then assess how the result changes with the conditions.

useCases.title: Which images need a closer look?
useCases.body: Test suitable processing against labelled material and route difficult cases to review. Do not assume the camera replaces an inspector.

useCases.title: Make the observation useful beyond the image.
useCases.body: Connect a suitable measurement or review result to a record, dashboard or operational workflow.

journey.heading: From a visual task to a measurement worth reviewing.
journey.example: A team wants to explore measuring fruit width from a camera image.
journey.question: Can the object boundary be measured consistently?
scope: Review when the edge is unclear
journey.boundary: Production grading and automatic rejection need separate validation and scope.

stages.label: Understand
stages.title: Define the visual task and collect the right examples.
stages.body: We discuss what needs measuring or identifying, inspect representative images and review how reference results are obtained. Camera position, scale, lighting and variation are part of the problem.
stages.output: A task definition, image set and reference approach.

stages.label: Agree
stages.title: Agree the prototype and what it must prove.
stages.body: The first scope explores width measurement under defined capture conditions. We agree calibration, relevant evaluation criteria and what happens when a measurement cannot be accepted.
stages.output: A prototype scope, capture requirements and evaluation plan.

stages.label: Build
stages.title: Make the calculation and overlay inspectable.
stages.body: A reviewable view shows the detected boundary and how a pixel measurement is converted using the reference scale. You can inspect the image and result together before considering a wider deployment.
stages.output: A focused prototype with traceable measurements.

stages.label: Test
stages.title: Compare with references and vary the conditions.
stages.body: We check representative images against reference measurements and inspect failure cases. Low contrast, occlusion or a changed scale must not silently produce a measurement presented as dependable.
stages.output: Evaluation results, observed limitations and review rules.

stages.label: Hand over
stages.title: Document what the setup can—and cannot—support.
stages.body: The handover covers capture conditions, calibration, evaluation evidence and maintenance needs. A production decision follows the results and any further work required, rather than the appearance of a convincing overlay.
stages.output: A setup guide, evaluation record and deployment decision inputs.

tests.label: Stable scale
tests.reason: This is the conversion to check against the reference measurement.

tests.label: Low contrast
tests.reason: Improve capture conditions or inspect the image before accepting a result.

tests.label: Scale changes
tests.reason: The previous pixel-to-millimetre scale should not be reused without a check.

handover.title: Capture & calibration
handover.body: Camera position, lighting, scale reference and calibration procedure.

handover.title: Evaluation & limitations
handover.body: Reference measurements, tested conditions and known failure cases.

handover.title: Next deployment decision
handover.body: Review workflow, maintenance needs and further validation before wider use.
